tagline: Home of the Bridge over the River Kwai, big waterfalls, the forested west, and riverside raft houses you can stay on all year
introHtml:
Kanchanaburi sits in the west of the country, about two hours from Bangkok past Nakhon Pathom to reach the town. The first thing most people picture is the Bridge over the River Kwai and the Death Railway — a World War II story still told through the museums, the Allied war cemetery, and the stretch of track that hugs the cliff at Tham Krasae to this day. The town itself is small but has plenty to walk around, both along the River Kwai and through the old quarter.

Outside town you reach the big forests of the west, with the seven-tier Erawan Falls, Sai Yok waterfalls, and the Srinagarind and Vajiralongkorn dams. Go deeper and you hit Sangkhla Buri, with its long wooden Mon Bridge and Mon community. People usually come to Kanchanaburi to sleep on a riverside raft house, run the rapids, see the waterfalls, then stop for river fish. It works for family trips, nature lovers, and anyone who wants to escape the city and spend a night or two by the water.
bestTime: November–February, when it's cool, the rain is gone, and the waterfalls still have water — the easiest time for the forest and for sleeping on a raft house

highlights.name: Bridge over the River Kwai
highlights.blurb: The steel railway bridge crossing the Kwai Yai in town — the icon of the province and the first thing people think of. You can walk across it and watch the train pass.

highlights.name: Death Railway and Tham Krasae
highlights.blurb: The wartime railway that runs along the cliffs beside the Kwai Noi. At Tham Krasae the train crosses a curved wooden trestle hugging the mountain — great views and a heavy history.

highlights.name: Erawan Falls
highlights.blurb: A seven-tier waterfall with emerald-green water in Erawan National Park. You can hike up and swim at each level — the waterfall most tied to Kanchanaburi.

highlights.name: River Kwai raft houses
highlights.blurb: The floating raft-house stays on the River Kwai are a signature of the province. Fall asleep to the sound of the water and jump in off the deck — the reason a lot of people stay the night here.

highlights.name: Sangkhla Buri and the Mon Bridge
highlights.blurb: The farthest district out west by the border, with the wooden Uttamanusorn Bridge across the lake, Wat Wang Wiwekaram, and a Mon way of life that feels different from anywhere else.

highlights.name: Allied war cemetery and war museums
highlights.blurb: A war cemetery in the middle of town and museums telling the story of the Death Railway and the prisoners of war — the place that makes the town's history make sense.

foodScene.name: River Kwai fish
foodScene.note: Fresh freshwater fish from the River Kwai — pla khang and pla yi sok — done as tom yum, grilled whole, or choo chee, at restaurants and raft houses around the province.

foodScene.name: Riverside spots and raft restaurants
foodScene.note: Restaurants along the River Kwai and floating rafts in town serve made-to-order dishes and river fish right on the water — the meal people come to Kanchanaburi to eat.

foodScene.name: Khao man som tam and Isan food
foodScene.note: Som tam, grilled chicken, and laap turn up all over town and along the road to the waterfalls — bold flavors that hit the spot after a full day of driving around.

foodScene.name: Noodles and town-market eats
foodScene.note: The markets and walking street in town have noodles, rice-and-curry, and snacks to graze on, especially in the evening down by the river.

foodScene.name: Sangkhla Buri Mon food
foodScene.note: The Sangkhla Buri area has Mon-style curries and snacks — gaeng hang lay, khanom jeen nam ya, and local sweets that are hard to find elsewhere.

foodScene.name: Mu kratha and dinner spots
foodScene.note: A go-to dinner for locals — plenty of mu kratha (DIY grill) places and casual eat-and-drink spots, relaxed and easy on the wallet.

foodScene.name: Riverside and hillside cafes
foodScene.note: New cafes keep opening in town, along the River Kwai, and on the way to the waterfalls — somewhere to sip a coffee with river and mountain views en route.

foodScene.name: Local souvenirs
foodScene.note: Thong muan, old-style sweets, and farm produce like pumpkin and corn are sold at the markets and roadside stalls to take home.

attractions.name: Bridge over the River Kwai
attractions.blurb: The steel railway bridge crossing the Kwai Yai in the middle of town — the symbol of the province. You can walk across it and watch the train pass.

attractions.name: Erawan National Park
attractions.blurb: A seven-tier waterfall with emerald-green water — hike up and swim at each level. The main waterfall people think of when they think of Kanchanaburi.

attractions.name: Sai Yok National Park
attractions.blurb: Forest and the Sai Yok Noi and Sai Yok Yai waterfalls beside the Kwai Noi, with caves, raft trips, and riverside places to stay overnight.

attractions.name: Tham Krasae and the Death Railway
attractions.blurb: The stretch of railway running along the cliffs beside the Kwai Noi — great views and a wartime story. Ride the train through it or take in the viewpoint on foot.

attractions.name: Srinagarind Dam
attractions.blurb: A big dam with a wide lake ringed by mountains, with viewpoints, boat trips, and riverside stays — good for anyone who likes water and mountain views.

attractions.name: Sangkhla Buri and the Mon Bridge
attractions.blurb: The wooden Uttamanusorn Bridge across the lake, Wat Wang Wiwekaram, and the Mon way of life in the farthest district out west.

attractions.name: Don Rak Allied War Cemetery
attractions.blurb: The Allied war cemetery in the center of town — quiet and well kept, a place to remember the history of the Death Railway.

attractions.name: Muang Sing and Prasat Muang Sing
attractions.blurb: A historical park with a Khmer-era stone temple beside the Kwai Noi — walk among the ruins in shady grounds.
